data:
This course introduces students to A/B testing in modern businesses. This topic has increased considerably in importance over the last decade, as entrepreneurs have learned to think creatively about how to generate data in more rigorous ways and as developments in information technology have facilitated the development of better data gathering. Key to this area is the insight that correlations do not imply causality and, in almost all cases, cannot measure impact. This course helps design and use experiments and natural experiments to measure impact. The class will assume no prior knowledge. However, some knowledge of statistics will be advantageous, and an interest in writing codes in R will be a bonus.
LEARNING OUTCOMES 
At the end of the course, the students would be able to learn: 
1. The difference between correlation and causation. 
2. Link theory with actionable business decision. 
3. Understand how AB tests work. 
4. Understand how analytics can shape business decisions.
